method: PRIMARILY OPEN AND QUOTED. Eight topic pages of ASHM's Australian STI Management Guidelines for Use in Primary Care, plus their What's New page, retrieved 2026-09-22 and QUOTED VERBATIM -- every pass claim is machine re-checkable against the retrieved files. This source is ENDORSED BY THE BBVSS and FUNDED BY THE AUSTRALIAN CENTRE FOR DISEASE CONTROL. It was retrieved because AMH's genital infections table points to it. ⚠️ IT CLOSES THE GONORRHOEA GAP that the compendium's drug-choice-for-selected-infections guideline flagged, AND IT CARRIES ACTUAL DOSES, which AMH's tables do not. ⚠️ THE SECOND SOURCE AMH POINTS TO -- the ASID Clostridioides difficile guidelines, Intern Med J 2025; 55(3): 503-13 -- IS CLOSED ACCESS AND WAS NOT RETRIEVED: Unpaywall is_oa false, oa_status closed, no PMC copy, publisher HTTP 403, all checked 2026-09-22. ONLY ITS PUBLIC PUBMED ABSTRACT IS HELD, which confirms the citation and the metronidazole-to-vancomycin change but gives NO DOSE and NO RECURRENCE ALGORITHM. An AJGP search for an open Australian C. difficile article found nothing. Five claims comparing this source with AMH are marked licensed_source_not_quoted because the AMH side of the comparison is paraphrased. ⚠️ CURRENCY: the gonorrhoea, genital herpes, cervicitis, epididymo-orchitis and urethritis pages appear in NEITHER the 2023-24 nor the 2024-25 minor-review list, so on the face of the What's New page their last revision was the 2020-2022 major review.

claims.claim: M. GENITALIUM AFTER MOXIFLOXACIN FAILS, from PUBLISHED CASE SERIES, SEEKING SPECIALIST ADVICE: PRISTINAMYCIN 1 G 3 TIMES DAILY WITH DOXYCYCLINE 100 MG TWICE DAILY FOR 10 DAYS, CURING 75% of macrolide-resistant infections, available through hospital pharmacies on the TGA SPECIAL ACCESS SCHEME; MINOCYCLINE 100 MG TWICE DAILY FOR 14 DAYS, CURING 70%, on private script; or DOXYCYCLINE 100 MG TWICE DAILY WITH SITAFLOXACIN 100 MG TWICE DAILY FOR 7 DAYS in cases who have failed all other therapies, with >90% EFFICACY, also Special Access Scheme

Cures 75% of macrolide-resistant infections. Pristinamycin is available through hospital pharmacies, using the Special Access Scheme of the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA). … Minocycline: 100 mg twice daily for 14 days. Cures 70% of macrolide-resistant infections. Minocycline is available on private script. … Combination therapy with doxycycline 100 mg twice daily and sitafloxacin 100 mg twice daily for 7 days.
